**Question**:

On 14th June 2023, long queues were observed at the electricity bill payment counters in city X.

**Reasons**:

 
• The deadline for paying electricity bills for City X is the 15th of every month.
 
• Due to server failure, many individuals were unable to pay their electricity bills online in June 2023.

options.text: Neither 1 or 2 are the incorrect reasons.

2. Due to server failure, many individuals were unable to pay their electricity bills online in June 2023: True (Because a server failure would prevent online payments, leading to more people paying their bills in person, thus causing long queues.)

So, both reasons are valid and justify the long queues observed at the electricity bill payment counters.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 2"**.

questions.question: Particles of matter are continuously moving due to their:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**kinetic energy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Kinetic energy is the energy that an object possesses due to its motion.
 
• All particles of matter are in constant motion, and this motion is a result of their kinetic energy.
 
• The temperature of a substance is a measure of the average kinetic energy of its particles.
 
• Increased kinetic energy results in faster movement of particles, which can lead to changes in the state of matter (e.g., from solid to liquid).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kinetic Energy:**

 
 
• Kinetic energy is a form of energy that an object or a particle has by reason of its motion.
 
• It is defined as the work needed to accelerate a body of a given mass from rest to its stated velocity.
 
• Once the object reaches this velocity, it maintains its kinetic energy unless its speed changes.
 
• The formula for kinetic energy (KE) is given by KE = 1/2 mv², where m is the mass and v is the velocity.
 
 
 
• **Other Forms of Energy:**
 
 
• **Nuclear Energy:** Energy released during nuclear fission or fusion, especially when used to generate electricity.
 
• **Chemical Energy:** Energy stored in the bonds of chemical compounds, released in a chemical reaction.
 
• **Mechanical Energy:** The sum of kinetic and potential energy in an object that is used to do work.
 
 
 
• **State of Matter:**
 
 
• Solid: Particles are closely packed and only vibrate in place.
 
• Liquid: Particles are close together but can move/slide past one another.
 
• Gas: Particles are far apart and move freely.
 
• Plasma: A state of matter similar to gas, but the particles are electrically charged.
 
 
 
• **Temperature and Kinetic Energy:**
 
 
• Temperature is a measure of the average kinetic energy of the particles in a substance.
 
• Higher temperatures correspond to higher average kinetic energies.
 
• As the temperature increases, the particles move faster, and thus the kinetic energy increases.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are related to ecosystem?

(i) It consists of biotic components comprising living organisms.

(ii) All green plants and certain bacteria are producers.

(iii) Decomposers break-down complex organic into simple organic substance.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3) Only (i) and (ii)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• An ecosystem comprises both biotic (living organisms) and abiotic (non-living elements) components.
 
• Green plants and certain bacteria are producers because they can manufacture their own food through photosynthesis or chemosynthesis.
 
• Decomposers, such as fungi and bacteria, break down dead organic matter into simpler inorganic substances, recycling nutrients back into the ecosystem.
 
• Statements (i) and (ii) are correct. Statement (iii) is incorrect because decomposers break down complex organic substances into simple inorganic substances, not organic.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ecosystem:**

 
 
• An ecosystem is a community of living organisms (plants, animals, and microbes) interacting with their physical environment (air, water, soil).
 
• It involves both biotic and abiotic components that interact as a system.
 
• Energy flows through an ecosystem in one direction—usually from the sun, through photosynthetic organisms (producers), to herbivores (consumers), and finally to decomposers.
 
 
 
• **Producers:**
 
 
• Producers, or autotrophs, are organisms that produce their own food through photosynthesis (using sunlight) or chemosynthesis (using chemical energy).
 
• Examples include green plants, algae, and certain bacteria.
 
 
 
• **Consumers:**
 
 
• Consumers, or heterotrophs, are organisms that cannot produce their own food and depend on other organisms for nutrition.
 
• They are categorized into primary consumers (herbivores), secondary consumers (carnivores that eat herbivores), and tertiary consumers (carnivores that eat other carnivores).
 
 
 
• **Decomposers:**
 
 
• Decomposers are organisms that break down dead or decaying organisms, and in doing so, carry out the natural process of decomposition.
 
• They play a critical role in nutrient cycling by converting organic materials back into inorganic substances, which can be used by producers.
 
• Examples include fungi, bacteria, and certain insects.

questions.question: Electric devices like laundry iron, electric toaster, electric oven, electric kettle and electric heater are based on which effect of electric current?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Heating effect**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The heating effect of electric current is utilized in devices like laundry iron, electric toaster, electric oven, electric kettle, and electric heater.
 
• When an electric current flows through a conductor, it produces heat due to the resistance to the flow of electrons in the conductor.
 
• The heat produced is directly proportional to the square of the current, the resistance of the conductor, and the time for which the current flows (Joule's law of heating).
 
• This principle is employed in various household appliances to generate heat for different purposes such as cooking, heating water, and ironing clothes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chemical effect of electric current**

 
 
• When an electric current passes through a conducting solution, it causes chemical reactions. This is known as the chemical effect of electric current.
 
• Examples include electroplating, electrolysis, and battery operation.
 
 
 
• **Magnetic effect of electric current**
 
 
• An electric current flowing through a wire creates a magnetic field around it. This is known as the magnetic effect of electric current.
 
• Applications include electric motors, generators, and transformers.
 
 
 
• **Physiological effect of electric current**
 
 
• The physiological effect refers to the impact of electric current on living tissues.
 
• Electric shocks, nerve stimulation, and muscle contractions are examples of physiological effects.

questions.question: A man loses 20% of his money. After spending 25% of the remaining amount, he has ₹480 left. What is the amount of money he originally had?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A man loses 20% of his money.

After spending 25% of the remaining amount, he has ₹480 left.

**Formula Used:**

Let the original amount be ₹x.

After losing 20% of his money, the remaining amount = x - 0.2x = 0.8x.

After spending 25% of the remaining amount, he has ₹480 left.

Remaining amount after spending 25% = 0.75 x 0.8x = 0.6x.

**Calculation:**

0.6x = 480

⇒ x = 480 / 0.6

⇒ x = 800

**The amount of money he originally had is ₹800.**

questions.question: The average of the first 25 multiples of 3 is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The first 25 multiples of 3.

**Formula Used:**

Average of n terms = Sum of n terms / n

Sum of first n multiples of a number = a × n(n+1)/2

**Calculation:**

Here, a = 3 and n = 25

Sum of the first 25 multiples of 3 = 3 × 25 × (25+1) / 2

Sum = 3 × 25 × 26 / 2

Sum = 3 × 325

Sum = 975

Average = Sum / n

Average = 975 / 25

Average = 39

**The average of the first 25 multiples of 3 is 39.**

questions.question: If 9.6 : 16.8 :: 18 : x, what is the value of x?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The given ratio is 9.6 : 16.8

Multiply both sides by 10 to remove decimals → 96 : 168

Divide by the common factor 24 to get the simplified ratio → 4 : 7

The second ratio 18 : x must be strictly equivalent to 4 : 7

If 4 parts = 18, then 1 part = 4.5

So, x = 7 parts = 7 × 4.5 = 31.5

**∴ The correct answer is 31.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The given proportion is 9.6 : 16.8 :: 18 : x

**Formula Used:**

For any proportion a : b :: c : d

Product of extreme terms = Product of mean terms

⇒ a × d = b × c

**Calculations:**

⇒ 9.6 × x = 16.8 × 18

⇒ x = (16.8 × 18) ÷ 9.6

⇒ Multiply the numerator and denominator by 10 to remove the decimal point:

⇒ x = (168 × 18) ÷ 96

⇒ Divide 168 and 96 by their greatest common divisor, 24:

Product Rule of Proportion

In any valid proportion a : b :: c : d, the product of extreme terms (a and d) is always mathematically equal to the product of mean terms (b and c).

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers a and c is defined as √(a × c), derived from the continued proportion a : b :: b : c.

Fourth Proportional

If four quantities satisfy the relation a : b :: c : d, then d is identified as the fourth proportional to a, b, and c.

questions.question: The amount of force needed to accelerate a 10 kg mass at 2.5m/s² is ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**25 N**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

To find the amount of force needed to accelerate a mass, we use** Newton's second law of motion**, which states: F= ma

Where:

__
 
• F is the force,
 
• m is the mass,
 
• a is the acceleration.

Given:

 
• m = 10 kg,
 
• a= 2.5 m/s²,

We can calculate F as follows:

 F=10 Kg times 2.5 m/s²= 25N

Therefore, the force needed is **25 N**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Force:**

 
 
• Force is an interaction that, when unopposed, will change the motion of an object.
 
• A force can cause an object with mass to change its velocity (which includes to begin moving from a state of rest), i.e., to accelerate.
 
• Force is a **vector **quantity, meaning it has** both magnitude and direction**.
 
 
 
• **Newton's Second Law of Motion:**
 
 
• It states that the force acting on an object is equal to the mass of the object times its acceleration ( F= ma).
 
• This law explains how the velocity of an object changes when it is subjected to an external force.
 
 
 
• **Mass:**
 
 
• Mass is a property of a physical body and a measure of its resistance to acceleration when a force is applied.
 
• The mass of an object also determines the strength of its gravitational attraction to other bodies.
 
 
 
• **Acceleration:**
 
 
• Acceleration is the rate of change in the velocity of an object with respect to time.
 
• It is a **vector **quantity, meaning it has both magnitude and direction.

questions.question: A 3-digit number is such that its units’ digit, tens’ digit and hundreds’ digit are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. The sum of this number and the number obtained by reversing its digits is 1332. Find the positive difference between the 3-digit number and the number formed by reversing its digit.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The digits of the 3-digit number are in the ratio 2:3:4.

The sum of the number and its reverse is 1332.

**Formula Used:**

Let the digits be 2x, 3x, and 4x.

The number can be represented as 100(4x) + 10(3x) + 2x.

The reverse number can be represented as 100(2x) + 10(3x) + 4x.

Sum of the number and its reverse = 1332.

**Calculation:**

Let the 3-digit number be 100(4x) + 10(3x) + 2x.

⇒ Number = 432x + 30x + 2x = 432x + 30x + 2x = 432x + 30x + 2x = 432x + 30x + 2x = 432x + 30x + 2x = 432x + 30x + 2x = 432x + 30x + 2x = 432x + 30x + 2x = 432x + 30x + 2x = 432x + 30x + 2x = 100(4x) + 10(3x) + 2x.

The reverse of the number is 100(2x) + 10(3x) + 4x.

⇒ Reverse Number = 200x + 30x + 4x = 200x + 30x + 4x = 234x.

The sum of the number and its reverse is 1332.

⇒ 432x + 234x = 1332.

⇒ 666x = 1332.

⇒ x = 1332 / 666.

⇒ x = 2.

So, the original number is 432x = 432 × 2 = 864.

And the reverse number is 234x = 234 × 2 = 468.

The positive difference between the original number and the reverse number is:

⇒ 864 - 468 = 396.

**The correct answer is option 3.**

questions.question: In case of jelly, which of the following is the dispersed phase?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Liquid phase**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In jelly, the dispersed phase is the **liquid phase** while the dispersion medium is the solid phase.
 
• Jelly is a type of **gel** where the liquid phase is dispersed in the solid network.
 
• The liquid phase in jelly provides the fluidity and moisture content of the gel.
 
• During the jelly-making process, the liquid phase solidifies upon cooling, forming a semi-solid structure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dispersed Phase:**

 
 
• The dispersed phase refers to the phase that is distributed or spread throughout another continuous phase known as the dispersion medium.
 
• In the context of colloids, the dispersed phase can be solid, liquid, or gas.
 
 
 
• **Dispersion Medium:**
 
 
• The dispersion medium is the continuous phase in which the dispersed phase is distributed.
 
• The dispersion medium can also be solid, liquid, or gas.
 
 
 
• **Colloids:**
 
 
• Colloids are mixtures where one substance is dispersed evenly throughout another without dissolving.
 
• Common types of colloids include gels, sols, emulsions, and foams.
 
 
 
• **Gel:**
 
 
• A gel is a colloidal system in which the dispersed phase is a liquid and the dispersion medium is a solid.
 
• Gels exhibit a semi-solid state and have properties of both solids and liquids.

questions.question: {If } x + (1)/(x) = 5, { then } x² + (1)/(x²) = ?

If x + 1/x = k, then x² + 1/x² = k² − 2

Given the value k = 5:

Value = 5² − 2

Value = 25 − 2 = 23

**∴ The correct answer is 23.**

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

**Calculation:**

⇒ (x + 1/x)² = 5²

⇒ x² + 1/x² + 2 × x × (1/x) = 25

⇒ x² + 1/x² + 2 = 25

⇒ x² + 1/x² = 25 − 2

⇒ x² + 1/x² = 23

questions.question: Which of the following is the characteristics of striated muscles?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**cylindrical, unbranched and multinucleate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Striated muscles are characterized by their **cylindrical shape**, which helps them to contract efficiently.
 
• They are **unbranched**, meaning the muscle fibers run parallel to each other without dividing.
 
• Striated muscle cells are **multinucleate**, containing multiple nuclei to support their high metabolic activity.
 
• These muscles are also known as **skeletal muscles** as they are usually attached to bones and facilitate movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Striated Muscles**

 
 
• Striated muscles, also known as skeletal muscles, are under voluntary control, which means we can consciously control their movements.
 
• They have a striped appearance due to the alternating dark and light bands, which are a result of the arrangement of actin and myosin filaments.
 
• These muscles are responsible for the body's movements, posture, and balance.
 
• Striated muscles are attached to bones by tendons, and they work in pairs to produce movement by contracting and relaxing.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ed061d04909ffe6b478cf54dee2ec8e52a4f696dd4614e09d9aa0587db1ffdb7.png] 

 
• **Smooth Muscles**

 
 
• Smooth muscles are found in the walls of internal organs such as the stomach, intestines, and blood vessels.
 
• They are involuntary muscles, meaning they operate without conscious control.
 
• Smooth muscles have a spindle-shaped, unbranched, and uninucleate structure, which allows them to contract slowly and sustain contractions for a long time.
 
 
 
• **Cardiac Muscles**
 
 
• Cardiac muscles are found only in the heart and are responsible for pumping blood throughout the body.
 
• They have a branched and striated appearance, similar to skeletal muscles, but they are involuntary like smooth muscles.
 
• Cardiac muscle cells are typically uninucleate, but they can also be binucleate.
 
• The cells are connected by intercalated discs, which allow for coordinated contractions and efficient heart function.

questions.question: Which of the following options represents metals that do NOT react with cold water?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aluminium, iron and zinc**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Aluminium, iron, and zinc** do not react with cold water.
 
• These metals require either hot water or steam to react, indicating a higher activation energy for the reaction.
 
• The reactivity of metals with water decreases as you move from top to bottom in the reactivity series.
 
• In general, metals like sodium and potassium react vigorously with cold water, while metals like aluminium, iron, and zinc do not.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reactivity Series:**

 
 
• The reactivity series is a series of metals, arranged in order of their reactivity from highest to lowest.
 
• Metals at the top of the series, such as potassium and sodium, are very reactive and can react with cold water.
 
• Metals lower in the series, such as aluminium, iron, and zinc, are less reactive and do not react with cold water.
 
 
 
• **Reaction with Water:**
 
 
• When metals react with water, they form a metal hydroxide and hydrogen gas.
 
• For example, sodium reacts with water to form sodium hydroxide and hydrogen gas.
 
• However, metals like aluminium, iron, and zinc require hot water or steam for such reactions to occur.
 
 
 
• **Activation Energy:**
 
 
• Activation energy is the minimum energy required for a chemical reaction to occur.
 
• Metals that do not react with cold water have a higher activation energy barrier that cold water cannot overcome.
 
• Therefore, higher temperatures are needed to provide the necessary energy for the reaction.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Reactions:**
 
 
• **Iron:** 3Fe + 4H₂O (steam) → Fe₃O₄ + 4H₂
 
• **Zinc:** Zn + H₂O (steam) → ZnO + H₂
 
• These reactions show that steam (not cold water) is required for these metals to react.

questions.question: Traits can be influenced by:

options.text: by both paternal DNA and maternal DNA

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**by both paternal DNA and maternal DNA**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Traits are inherited from both **paternal (father's) DNA** and **maternal (mother's) DNA**.
 
• Each parent contributes 50% of the DNA, which combines to form the unique genetic makeup of an individual.
 
• The combination of maternal and paternal DNA influences the traits and characteristics of the offspring.
 
• This process of inheritance follows the principles of **Mendelian genetics**, which explains how traits are passed from parents to offspring.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **DNA (Deoxyribonucleic Acid)**

 
 
• DNA is a molecule that contains the genetic instructions used in the growth, development, functioning, and reproduction of all known living organisms and many viruses.
 
• It is composed of two strands that coil around each other to form a double helix.
 
• Each strand is made up of a sequence of four types of nucleotides: adenine (A), thymine (T), cytosine (C), and guanine (G).
 
 
 
• **Genes**
 
 
• Genes are segments of DNA that carry hereditary information.
 
• They are responsible for the inherited traits and characteristics of an organism.
 
• Each gene occupies a specific location on a chromosome.
 
 
 
• **Chromosomes**
 
 
• Chromosomes are long DNA molecules with part or all of the genetic material of an organism.
 
• Humans have 23 pairs of chromosomes, for a total of 46.
 
• One set of 23 chromosomes is inherited from the mother, and the other set is inherited from the father.
 
 
 
• **Mendelian Genetics**
 
 
• Gregor Mendel, the father of genetics, discovered the basic principles of heredity through experiments with pea plants.
 
• Mendelian genetics explains how traits are inherited through the interaction of alleles, which are different forms of a gene.
 
• Traits can be dominant or recessive, and the combination of alleles from both parents determines the traits of the offspring.

Average speed = Total distance travelled / Total time

**Calculation:**

Total distance = 3 km + 3 km + 3 km + 3 km = 12 km

Time taken for the second 3 km = 3 / 20 = 0.15 hours

questions.question: A series of compounds in which the same functional group substitutes for hydrogen in a carbon chain is called ____________.

__
 
• A homologous series is a group of organic compounds that have the same functional group and similar chemical properties.
 
• In a homologous series, each successive compound differs by a CH₂ unit.
 
• Members of a homologous series show a gradual change in physical properties, such as boiling and melting points.
 
• Examples of homologous series include alkanes, alkenes, and alkynes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Catenation is the ability of an element to form bonds with other atoms of the same element, leading to the formation of chains or rings.
 
• This property is commonly seen in carbon, which can form long chains and complex structures.
 
• Examples include diamond and graphite, which are allotropes of carbon.
 
 
 
• **Isomers:**
 
 
• Isomers are compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural arrangements.
 
• There are different types of isomers, such as structural isomers and stereoisomers.
 
• Structural isomers have different connectivity of atoms, while stereoisomers have the same connectivity but differ in spatial arrangement.
 
 
 
• **Heterologous series:**
 
 
• Heterologous series is not a standard term in organic chemistry and might be a confusion with "heteroatoms" which refers to atoms other than carbon and hydrogen in an organic molecule.
 
• Common heteroatoms include oxygen, nitrogen, sulfur, and halogens.

__
 
• The peripheral nervous system (PNS) consists of the nerves and ganglia outside the brain and spinal cord.
 
• The PNS includes cranial nerves, which emerge directly from the brain, and spinal nerves, which emerge from segments of the spinal cord.
 
• The PNS connects the central nervous system (CNS) to the limbs and organs.
 
• The primary function of the PNS is to relay information between the CNS and the rest of the body.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Central Nervous System (CNS)**

 
 
• The CNS consists of the brain and spinal cord.

questions.question: Water flows into a tank having the dimensions of its base given as 200 m × 150 m through a rectangular pipe having dimensions given as 1.5 m × 1.25 m @ 20 kmph. In what time (in minutes) will the water rise by 2 meters?

**Given:**

Dimensions of the tank's base = 200 m × 150 m

Dimensions of the rectangular pipe = 1.5 m × 1.25 m

Speed of water flow = 20 kmph

Required water rise = 2 meters

**Formula Used:**

Volume of water required = Base area of tank × Required rise in water level

Volume of water flow per hour = Cross-sectional area of pipe × Speed of water flow

Time required (in hours) = Volume of water required / Volume of water flow per hour

**Calculation:**

Base area of the tank = 200 m × 150 m = 30000 m²

Volume of water required = 30000 m² × 2 m = 60000 m³

Cross-sectional area of the pipe = 1.5 m × 1.25 m = 1.875 m²

Speed of water flow = 20 kmph = 20000 m / 60 min = 20000 / 60 m/min

Volume of water flow per minute = 1.875 m² × 20000 / 60 m/min

Volume of water flow per minute = 625 m³/min

Time required (in minutes) = Volume of water required / Volume of water flow per minute

⇒ Time required = 60000 m³ / 625 m³/min

⇒ Time required = 96 minutes

**The correct answer is option 2 (96 minutes).**

• The principal focus is a point on the principal axis from which the reflected rays seem to originate.
 
• In a convex mirror, the principal focus is virtual, meaning it cannot be reached physically as it is located behind the mirror.
 
• This property of convex mirrors makes them useful for applications such as rearview mirrors in vehicles, where they provide a wider field of view.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Convex Mirror**

 
 
• A convex mirror is a spherical mirror in which the reflective surface bulges outward.
 
 
• **Principal Focus**
 
 
• The principal focus (F) of a mirror is the point where parallel rays of light either converge or appear to diverge after reflecting from the mirror.
 
• For a convex mirror, the principal focus is virtual and lies behind the mirror.
 
• The distance between the mirror and the principal focus is known as the focal length (f).
 
 
 
• **Reflection of Light**
 
 
• Reflection is the phenomenon where light rays bounce off a surface.
 
• The law of reflection states that the angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection.
 
• In the case of spherical mirrors, the direction of the incident and reflected rays can be predicted using ray diagrams.
 
 
 
• **Ray Diagrams**
 
 
• Ray diagrams are graphical methods to trace the path of light rays reflecting from mirrors or passing through lenses.
 
• They help in understanding the formation and nature of the image produced by mirrors and lenses.
 
• Key rays used in ray diagrams for mirrors include the parallel ray (which reflects through the focal point), the focal ray (which reflects parallel to the principal axis), and the center of curvature ray (which reflects back along its own path).

questions.question: The sum of two numbers is 36. Five times one number is equal to 4 times the other. The greater of the two numbers is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The sum of two numbers is 36.

Five times one number is equal to 4 times the other.

**Formula Used:**

Let the two numbers be x and y.

Equation 1: x + y = 36

Equation 2: 5x = 4y

**Calculation:**

From Equation 2: 5x = 4y

⇒ y = 5x/4

Substitute y in Equation 1:

⇒ x + 5x/4 = 36

⇒ (4x + 5x)/4 = 36

⇒ 9x/4 = 36

⇒ 9x = 144

⇒ x = 144/9

⇒ x = 16

Substitute x in Equation 1:

⇒ 16 + y = 36

⇒ y = 36 - 16

⇒ y = 20

**The greater of the two numbers is 20.**

• It operates on the principle of magnetism and does not utilize the magnetic effects of electric current.

questions.question: Which cell organelle is associated with generation of ATP?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mitochondria**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Mitochondria are known as the **powerhouses of the cell** because they generate most of the cell's supply of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), which is used as a source of chemical energy.
 
• They are **double-membrane-bound organelles** found in most eukaryotic organisms.
 
• The inner membrane of the mitochondrion is folded into structures known as **cristae**, which increase the surface area for ATP production.
 
• Mitochondria have their own **DNA and ribosomes**, and are believed to have originated from free-living prokaryotes through endosymbiosis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lysosomes**

 
 
• These are membrane-bound organelles that contain enzymes responsible for breaking down waste materials and cellular debris.
 
• They are often referred to as the "digestive system" of the cell because they help in the degradation of macromolecules.
 
 
 
• **Chloroplast**
 
 
• These are organelles found in plant cells and eukaryotic algae that conduct photosynthesis.
 
• Chloroplasts capture light energy and convert it into chemical energy in the form of glucose through the process of photosynthesis.
 
 
 
• **Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER)**
 
 
• It is a network of membranes within the cytoplasm of eukaryotic cells, involved in protein and lipid synthesis.
 
• The ER is divided into two types: rough ER (with ribosomes) and smooth ER (without ribosomes).
 
• Rough ER is involved in protein synthesis and folding, while smooth ER is associated with lipid synthesis and detoxification processes.

questions.question: Dr. Shankarbaba Pundlikrao Papalkar is known for his dedication to improving the lives of:
questions.solution:

__
 
• Dr. Shankarbaba Pundlikrao Papalkar is renowned for his dedication to improving the lives of **disabled and destitute children**.
 
• He has been actively involved in providing education, healthcare, and rehabilitation services to these children.
 
• His efforts have led to the establishment of several institutions and support systems specifically aimed at the welfare of disabled and destitute children.
 
• Through his initiatives, many disabled and destitute children have been able to lead better lives and integrate into mainstream society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Disabled Children**

 
 
• Disabled children are those who have physical, sensory, intellectual, or developmental impairments that can affect their ability to participate in typical educational and social activities.
 
• They may require special education services, assistive technologies, and tailored healthcare interventions to enhance their quality of life.
 
• Organizations and individuals working for disabled children often focus on providing inclusive education, early intervention programs, and vocational training.
 
• Support systems for disabled children aim to empower them to achieve their full potential and lead independent lives.
 
 
 
• **Destitute Children**
 
 
• Destitute children are those who lack basic necessities such as food, shelter, and parental care due to extreme poverty, abandonment, or loss of parents.
 
• They are highly vulnerable and often require immediate intervention to ensure their safety and well-being.
 
• Programs for destitute children typically include provision of shelter homes, nutritional support, educational opportunities, and psychological counseling.
 
• Efforts are made to rehabilitate these children by reuniting them with family members if possible or by providing long-term care solutions such as adoption or foster care.
 
 
 
• **Rehabilitation Services**
 
 
• Rehabilitation services for children with disabilities and those in destitute situations include medical, psychological, social, and educational interventions aimed at improving their overall functioning.
 
• These services help children develop essential life skills, improve mobility, and enhance their ability to communicate and interact with others.
 
• Rehabilitation may involve physical therapy, speech therapy, occupational therapy, and counseling.
 
• The goal is to enable these children to lead fulfilling lives and integrate into their communities.
 
 
 
• **Inclusive Education**
 
 
• Inclusive education is an approach that seeks to educate all children, regardless of their abilities or socio-economic background, in a common learning environment.
 
• It promotes equality and participation by ensuring that every child has access to quality education.
 
• Inclusive education involves adapting teaching methods, curricula, and learning environments to meet the diverse needs of all students.
 
• This approach helps in breaking down barriers and fostering a culture of acceptance and respect for differences among students.
